name: Homegrown Blister Wash 'Shelf Special'
description:
No manufacturer. No registration. No safety data sheet. The Shelf Special is a category of improvised chemical spray assembled from industrial cleaning solvents, agricultural concentrates, and chemical precursors available through Meridian Municipal Supply's open-market distribution channels or salvaged from the industrial waste streams that flow through the Shelf's sub-level infrastructure. Formulas vary by maker and availability — the most common variants combine concentrated industrial degreaser base with either agricultural-grade capsaicin extract, phenol derivative rinse concentrate, or in more dangerous iterations, trace oxidizing agents recovered from battery recycling operations. The result is delivered in repurposed pressurized containers: cleaning spray bottles, modified aerosol cans, or improvised pump chambers made from scavenged plumbing components.

The effects of a Shelf Special are unpredictable in the truest sense. A batch made with degreaser and agricultural capsaicin produces an extremely aggressive OC-like effect with significantly deeper tissue penetration than commercial sprays — the industrial solvent carrier strips protective oils and drives the active compound into the dermis rather than sitting on the surface. A batch incorporating phenol derivatives produces chemical burns with delayed onset — a subject may not realize the severity of exposure for several minutes. Batches that include oxidizing agents or improperly neutralized industrial acids have produced outcomes ranging from severe chemical burns to respiratory failure. Makers rarely know exactly what they have until it is used.

The Shelf Special is not a product. It is a symptom — of poverty, of the reality that Tier 1 residents cannot access licensed self-defense tools, and of the chemical abundance of an industrial city whose waste products are more accessible to its poorest residents than its consumer goods. Law enforcement treats possession as a serious offense. Street medics treat exposure as a major emergency.
legality: Prohibited — manufacture and possession of unlicensed chemical weapons; enforcement is aggressive in all tiers above Tier 1, inconsistent within Tier 1 itself
specifications:
Composition: variable (maker-dependent; no standardization)
Common bases: industrial degreaser, phenol derivative concentrate, agricultural OC extract
Delivery: improvised pressurized container (repurposed aerosol, pump spray, modified plumbing)
Effective range: 0.5–2m (container-dependent)
Onset: 2–30 seconds (compound-dependent)
Duration of effect: 20 minutes to permanent (compound-dependent)
Lethality risk: present and unquantifiable; respiratory failure documented in phenol/oxidizer variants
Cost: Φ8–Φ25 in materials
tactical_use: Used almost exclusively in Tier 1 personal defense and territorial conflict — the Shelf Special is a last resort for people who have no legal recourse and no access to licensed tools. It is deployed at extremely close range given the limitations of improvised delivery vessels. The lack of predictability cuts both ways: a maker who has produced a particularly effective batch may not be able to replicate it, and a user cannot know whether they are holding a painful inconvenience or a potentially lethal chemical weapon until they use it. Street medics advise anyone exposed to treat it as a chemical burn regardless of initial presentation.
cultural_context: The Shelf Special occupies a complex cultural position in Tier 1 communities — simultaneously a symbol of resourcefulness and a symbol of desperation. Making a good batch requires real chemical knowledge, and respected makers in tight-knit Shelf communities are sometimes called 'chemists' without irony. At the same time, the product exists because its users cannot access anything better, and everyone who uses it knows it. 'Shelf Special' said in mixed company is a class marker as much as a product description. The phrase 'Poor Man's Flense' draws a direct comparison to the Arcturus NS-3 — the same pain, the same helplessness, but one sold by a corporation and one made in a sink.
known_users: desperate individuals with no legal defensive options
story_hooks: A street medic has been seeing an unusual cluster of severe respiratory cases in a three-block radius — someone in the area is making Shelf Special with a particularly dangerous oxidizer component, and they don't know it
